identity.title: ALMA Observations of the Outflow from Source I in the Orion-KL Region

paper_type_evidence.quote: we present sensitive millimeter SiO (J=5-4; $\nu$=0) line observations of the outflow arising from the enigmatic object Orion Source I made with the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA).

evidence.quote: The phase reference center for the observations was at $\alpha_{J2000.0}$ = $05^{\rm h}35^{\rm m}14\mbox{$^{\rm s}\mskip-7.6mu.\,$}35$, $\delta_{J2000.0}$ = $-05^{\circ}22'35\mbox{$''\mskip-7.6mu.\,$}00$.

question.value: What are the morphology and velocity structure of the large-scale SiO outflow from Orion Source I, and how do they compare with the small-scale maser kinematics?

evidence.quote: contrary to what is found in the SiO and H$_2$O maser observations at scales of tens of AU, the blueshifted radial velocities of the moving gas are found to the northwest, while the redshifted velocities are in the southeast.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA Science Verification data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00009.SV

evidence.quote: with the blueshifted radial velocities found to the northwest, while the redshifted velocities are toward the southeast.
